exercises.name: 90/90 Hip Switch
exercises.setup: Sit on the floor with both knees bent at ninety degrees, one leg in front and one out to the side, hands behind you for support.
exercises.swingRationale: Locked-up hip internal rotation is why the lead hip stalls and the hands take over through impact.

exercises.name: Open Book
exercises.setup: Lie on your side with knees stacked and bent toward your chest, arms straight out in front at shoulder height.
cues: Follow your hand with your eyes
exercises.swingRationale: A t-spine that will not rotate forces the arms to disconnect from the turn, steepening the downswing and causing fat contact.

exercises.name: Quadruped T-Spine Rotation
exercises.setup: Get on hands and knees, place one hand behind your head with the elbow pointing out to the side.
exercises.swingRationale: Restricted thoracic rotation shortens the backswing and pushes golfers to sway laterally instead of turning for width.

exercises.name: World's Greatest Stretch
exercises.setup: Start in a long lunge with your front foot forward, back knee off the floor, both hands inside the front foot.
cues: Keep front knee stacked over ankle
exercises.swingRationale: Combines the hip and thoracic mobility golfers need to complete a full backswing turn without early extension.

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Ankle Rock
exercises.setup: Kneel on one knee with the other foot flat on the floor in front, hands resting on the front thigh.
cues: Drive the front knee over toes
exercises.swingRationale: A front ankle that cannot dorsiflex forces the lead knee to slide instead of stabilize, leaking power at impact.

exercises.name: Club-Behind-Back Shoulder Turn
exercises.setup: Stand in your golf posture with a club held horizontally across your shoulder blades, both forearms resting on top.
cues: Feel the stretch across the chest
exercises.swingRationale: Isolates shoulder turn from hip turn, the separation that creates torque instead of an all-arms swing.

exercises.name: Club Overhead Side Bend
exercises.setup: Stand tall holding a club overhead with both hands wide, feet shoulder-width apart.
exercises.swingRationale: Frees the lat and side-bend range that lets the trail shoulder drop under the ball instead of steepening the swing.

exercises.name: Seated Figure Four
exercises.setup: Sit tall in a chair, cross one ankle over the opposite knee, keeping the crossed foot flexed.
cues: Press the crossed knee down gently
exercises.swingRationale: Tight glutes limit hip turn on the backswing, a common cause of reverse pivots and thin contact.

exercises.name: Couch Stretch
exercises.setup: Kneel in front of a wall or couch with your back shin resting against it, front foot planted ahead of you.
cues: Hold, breathe, do not force it
exercises.swingRationale: A short hip flexor blocks the trail hip from extending fully through impact, robbing speed and forcing the low back to compensate.

exercises.name: Cat-Cow
exercises.setup: Get on hands and knees with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips.
exercises.swingRationale: Warms the spine through its full range so early reps of the swing do not ask a cold back for rotation it is not ready to give.

exercises.name: Band Shoulder Pass-Through
exercises.setup: Stand holding a band with a wide overhand grip in front of your thighs.
exercises.swingRationale: Builds the overhead shoulder mobility that keeps the trail arm connected at the top instead of collapsing the backswing.

exercises.name: Wall Slide
exercises.setup: Stand with your back, head and arms against a wall, elbows and wrists touching it at ninety degrees.
exercises.swingRationale: Improves scapular control that keeps the lead arm on plane instead of disconnecting from the chest in transition.

exercises.name: Deep Squat Hold
exercises.setup: Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulders, lower into the deepest squat you can hold with heels flat.
exercises.swingRationale: Hips and ankles that cannot sit into a squat are why golfers stand up out of posture on the way down, turning a solid strike into a thin, bladed shot.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Lowering
exercises.setup: Lie on your back with both legs straight up toward the ceiling, low back flat on the floor.
exercises.swingRationale: Trains hamstring length and pelvic control that keep your spine angle steady instead of standing up out of the shot.

exercises.name: Standing Hamstring Sweep
exercises.setup: Stand tall, extend one leg out in front with the heel on the ground, hands resting on the other thigh.
cues: Hinge at the hips, flat back
exercises.swingRationale: Tight hamstrings limit the forward hip hinge at address, pushing golfers into a hunched, arms-only posture.

exercises.name: Thread the Needle
exercises.setup: Start on hands and knees, then slide one arm underneath your body, palm up, resting your shoulder and ear on the floor.
cues: Feel the stretch between shoulder blades
exercises.swingRationale: Opens the upper back rotation needed to keep the club on plane instead of pulling it across the line.

exercises.name: Band Rotational Punch
exercises.setup: Anchor a band at chest height behind you, stand side-on in your golf posture and hold the handle at your sternum.
exercises.swingRationale: Trains the ground-up sequence that produces clubhead speed instead of an arms-only lash at the ball.

exercises.name: Band Chop
exercises.setup: Anchor a band high above one shoulder, stand side-on and hold the handle with both hands extended overhead.
cues: Pull down and across the body
Finish low near the opposite hip
exercises.swingRationale: Builds the downward chest rotation that delivers the club on plane instead of casting it from the top.

exercises.name: Band Lift
exercises.setup: Anchor a band low near the floor, stand side-on and hold the handle with both hands at the opposite hip.
cues: Pull up and across the body
Rotate from the trunk, not arms
exercises.swingRationale: Mirrors the upward path of the follow-through, training rotational speed through the ball instead of just arm swing.

exercises.name: Band Hip Snap
exercises.setup: Anchor a band low behind you, loop it around your hips, and stand in an athletic hinge facing away from the anchor.
exercises.swingRationale: Trains the explosive hip extension that generates ground-up speed instead of relying on arms to hit the ball hard.

exercises.name: Club Speed Swing
exercises.setup: Stand in your golf posture holding a lightweight club, feet set as if playing a normal shot.
cues: Swing to full speed through impact
exercises.swingRationale: Overspeed reps teach the body to sequence hips, torso, then arms, the pattern that adds distance without losing control.

exercises.name: Reverse Club Speed Swing
exercises.setup: Stand in your golf posture holding a lightweight club, set up for a normal swing but mirrored to the opposite side.
exercises.swingRationale: Trains the rotational direction most golfers never load, so power is built on both sides instead of just the dominant swing pattern.

exercises.name: Jump Squat
exercises.setup: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, arms relaxed at your sides.
exercises.swingRationale: Builds the vertical ground force that underlies rotational clubhead speed, the same power source used from address to impact.

exercises.name: Split Jump
exercises.setup: Start in a staggered lunge stance, front knee bent, back heel lifted.
cues: Land soft in the opposite stance
exercises.swingRationale: Develops single-leg power and landing control that mirror the weight transfer from trail to lead side through impact.

exercises.name: Broad Jump
exercises.setup: Stand with feet hip-width apart, knees slightly bent, arms back ready to swing forward.
cues: Swing arms forward as you jump
exercises.swingRationale: Trains horizontal force production, the same forward drive that powers the push off the ground into impact.

exercises.name: Lateral Bound
exercises.setup: Stand on one leg with a slight knee bend, the other leg lifted out to the side.
cues: Land soft on the opposite leg
exercises.swingRationale: Builds the lateral-to-rotational force transfer that stops the hips from sliding instead of turning through the ball.

exercises.name: Skater Hop
exercises.setup: Stand on one leg with a soft knee bend, torso slightly forward, other leg trailing behind.
cues: Hop sideways to the other foot
exercises.swingRationale: Trains quick lateral power and single-leg stability that support a stable trail-side push into the downswing.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.setup: Get into a plank position with hands slightly wider than shoulders, body in one straight line.
exercises.swingRationale: Pressing strength stabilizes the lead arm and chest through impact instead of letting the club face flip closed.

exercises.name: Tempo Push-Up
exercises.setup: Get into a plank position with hands slightly wider than shoulders, body in one straight line.
cues: Lower for a slow four count
exercises.swingRationale: Slow eccentric control builds the tissue resilience that keeps posture from breaking down late in a round.

exercises.name: Single-Arm-Biased Push-Up
exercises.setup: Get into a wide plank, one hand under the shoulder and the other hand walked out toward that side.
cues: Shift most of the load to one arm
exercises.swingRationale: Builds the asymmetric pressing strength that stabilizes the lead side against the club's momentum through the ball.

exercises.name: Band Row
exercises.setup: Anchor a band at chest height in front of you, step back to create tension, and hold a handle in each hand.
cues: Keep chest up, do not lean
exercises.swingRationale: Upper-back pulling strength counters the pressing dominance of the swing, protecting posture from rounding forward over time.

exercises.name: Band Pull-Apart
exercises.setup: Stand tall holding a light band with both hands at shoulder height, arms extended in front.
cues: Pull the band apart to your chest
exercises.swingRationale: Strengthens the rear shoulder muscles that hold the club face square at the top instead of letting it collapse.

exercises.name: Band Face Pull
exercises.setup: Anchor a band at face height, step back for tension, and hold a handle in each hand at arm's length.
cues: Rotate palms forward at the finish
exercises.swingRationale: Builds rotator cuff and rear-shoulder strength that keeps the trail shoulder from rounding forward at address.

exercises.name: Kneeling Band Pulldown
exercises.setup: Kneel facing away from a high anchor point, hold the band overhead with both hands.
cues: Pull elbows down to your sides
exercises.swingRationale: Trains lat engagement that connects the arms to the torso, preventing a disconnected chicken-wing at the top.

exercises.name: Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
exercises.setup: Stand a stride length in front of a chair, step or couch, rest the top of your back foot on it, front foot flat ahead.
exercises.swingRationale: Builds single-leg strength in the lead leg, the post it braces against during the downswing to resist collapsing.

exercises.name: Single-Leg RDL
exercises.setup: Stand tall on one leg with a soft bend in the knee, arms relaxed and free at your sides.
cues: Hinge forward, extend the back leg
Keep hips square to the floor
Reach the free hand toward the floor
exercises.swingRationale: Trains single-leg hip hinge strength and balance, the exact demand placed on the trail leg during the backswing.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge
exercises.setup: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, hands resting on your hips.
cues: Lower the back knee toward the floor
exercises.swingRationale: A lead knee that buckles inward instead of holding firm is why contact goes fat or thin instead of ball-then-turf.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
exercises.setup: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat on the floor hip-width apart.
exercises.swingRationale: Builds glute strength that drives hip extension through impact instead of leaving the low back to do that work.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.setup: Lie on your back with one knee bent and foot flat, the other leg extended straight up.
cues: Squeeze the glute at the top
exercises.swingRationale: Isolates one-sided glute strength, correcting the imbalance that lets the trail hip collapse instead of driving into impact.

exercises.name: Wall Sit
exercises.setup: Lean your back against a wall and slide down until your knees are bent near ninety degrees.
cues: Press low back into the wall
exercises.swingRationale: Builds the isometric leg endurance that keeps your posture from rising up late in a round of walking golf.

exercises.name: Calf Raise
exercises.setup: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, holding a wall or rail lightly for balance.
cues: Rise onto the balls of your feet
exercises.swingRationale: A trail foot that rolls off the inside edge on the way down leaks the ground force that would have gone into ball speed.

exercises.name: Band Anti-Rotation Press
exercises.setup: Anchor a band at chest height to the side, stand perpendicular to it and hold the handle at your sternum with both hands.
cues: Press straight out from the chest
Resist the band's pull to rotate
exercises.swingRationale: Builds the core stability to resist unwanted rotation, keeping the swing sequence from unwinding too early from the top.

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.setup: Lie on your side propped up on one forearm, elbow under the shoulder, legs stacked and straight.
cues: Keep body in one straight line
exercises.swingRationale: Trains lateral core strength that resists the side bend forces of the swing, protecting the low back from strain.

exercises.name: Copenhagen Plank
exercises.setup: Lie on your side, top foot resting on a chair, step or couch, bottom leg tucked behind, propped up on your bottom forearm.
cues: Lift the bottom leg to meet the top
exercises.swingRationale: Builds inner-thigh and hip strength that stabilizes the trail leg against the lateral forces of the downswing.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.setup: Lie on your back with arms reaching toward the ceiling and knees bent at ninety degrees above your hips.
cues: Press low back into the floor
Extend opposite arm and leg slowly
exercises.swingRationale: Trains the core to hold a stable spine while limbs move, mirroring how the trunk resists the arms during the swing.

exercises.name: Bird Dog
exercises.setup: Get on hands and knees with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips.
exercises.swingRationale: Builds the anti-rotation core strength that keeps the spine stable while the arms and legs move independently through the swing.

exercises.name: Hollow Hold
exercises.setup: Lie on your back, arms extended overhead, legs straight, low back pressed into the floor.
cues: Reach long through fingers and toes
exercises.swingRationale: Builds the whole-body core tension that keeps the spine angle set from address through a fast release.

exercises.name: Front Plank Reach
exercises.setup: Get into a forearm plank with elbows under shoulders, body in one straight line.
exercises.swingRationale: Trains anti-rotation core control, resisting the twist that leaks power and opens the club face early.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Balance with Club Reach
exercises.setup: Stand on one leg holding a club vertically in the opposite hand, standing tall with a slight knee bend.
exercises.swingRationale: Builds the single-leg stability that lets the lead leg brace firmly through impact instead of buckling.

exercises.name: Standing Hip Airplane
exercises.setup: Stand on one leg with a slight knee bend, torso hinged forward, arms out to the sides like a T.
cues: Hold torso steady over the leg
exercises.swingRationale: Trains hip rotation control on a single stable leg, mirroring the trail-hip stability needed at the top of the backswing.

programs.title: Mobility Foundations
programs.subtitle: Turn further without forcing it
programs.whoThisIsFor: Start here if you cannot make a full backswing without lifting your lead heel or sliding off the ball. Four weeks of hips, mid-back and ankles, three short sessions a week, no equipment beyond a band and a club.

prescriptions.note: Pause two seconds at the end of each switch.

programs.title: Off-Season Power
programs.subtitle: Build the speed you play with next season
programs.whoThisIsFor: Move here once mobility is no longer the limit and you want to build the rotational speed, single-leg strength and pressing power that turn a good off-season into more distance next spring. Eight weeks, three sessions a week, a band and a club is all you need.

programs.title: In-Season Maintenance
programs.subtitle: Keep what you built, stay fresh for Saturday
programs.whoThisIsFor: For the season itself: two short sessions a week that hold the power and strength you built in the off-season without leaving you sore for your round. Repeat this block for as long as you're playing.
